nodes.label: ICRR Journal Public Website
nodes.rationale: Ten public views for the International Collegiate Research Review, an independent open-access journal publishing undergraduate and graduate research across five sections. Built on Next.js App Router, TypeScript strict, Tailwind v4 with CSS-first @theme tokens.

nodes.label: Content Layer (src/lib/content/)
nodes.rationale: No page imports a data source directly. Each accessor picks Supabase or the seed files at call time, and each is wrapped in React's cache, so a render that asks for the site config in the layout and again in the page pays for one query. Keeps the data source swappable and access rules in one place.

nodes.label: Prerendered Public Pages
nodes.rationale: Every public page shows the same thing to everybody, so none needs to be built per visit. One cookies() call anywhere in a render marks the whole route dynamic, and reading content through the request-bound Supabase client used to do exactly that on every page. Pages refresh on a five-minute timer, and the admin calls revalidatePath('/', 'layout') on save so an edit is live immediately. Playwright must build, not just serve, because CONTENT_SOURCE=seed has to be set for the build that writes the HTML.

nodes.label: Cookieless Anon Supabase Client (src/lib/supabase/public.ts)
nodes.rationale: Exists precisely to keep public routes static: content reads must not touch cookies(), which would mark the route dynamic.

nodes.label: useFormFields Hook (form state retention)
nodes.rationale: Every public form field is React state so a rejected submission comes back filled in with only the bad fields marked. React empties a form once its action returns, and it restores a controlled text input afterwards but not a <select> or a checkbox, so the hook puts those two back itself. Lives in src/components/ui/FieldError.tsx.

nodes.label: ImageSlot Component
nodes.rationale: A null path produces an on-brand labelled placeholder, so filling a slot is a data change rather than a code change. Paths always come from content data, never JSX literals.

nodes.label: Three Client Islands
nodes.rationale: Server components by default; only the nav (matchMedia variant switching and drawer), the authors browser, and the toast provider carry interactivity. The announcement bar used to be a fourth island; it now slides in CSS and holds no state.

nodes.label: Direct-to-Storage Manuscript Upload
nodes.rationale: A manuscript can be 20 MB and a Server Action cannot carry one: Next caps the body at 1 MB and raising it only moves the wall, because on Netlify these actions run as functions whose request payload limit is a few megabytes whatever Next allows. So the file never passes through the server. next.config.ts still raises serverActions.bodySizeLimit to 10 MB for the admin media library, the one remaining path where the deploy target's payload limit applies.

nodes.label: createManuscriptUpload
nodes.rationale: Checks the form, then signs a one-time upload URL for a single path in the manuscripts bucket; the browser uploads to storage directly.

nodes.label: submitManuscript
nodes.rationale: Handed the storage path, confirms the object arrived and is within size, and records the row. Validates the same fields as createManuscriptUpload because it is reachable on its own. If the insert fails, the object is removed again.

nodes.label: Three Enforced Copy Rules
nodes.rationale: No em dashes; never 'Editorial Board'; and no claim to a review model the journal does not run. The ethics page says a submission is 'reviewed' and never says by how many people or under what blinding. Enforced by tests/unit/design-audit.test.ts, which scans source with comments stripped so a comment may name the banned phrasing to explain it.

nodes.label: Two Visual Constraints (no radius, one shadow)
nodes.rationale: No border radius anywhere except the announcement dot and the timeline rail dots, and exactly one shadow in the whole design, on the toast.

nodes.label: Policy Pages (/privacy, /terms, /ethics)
nodes.rationale: Written to match what the site actually does rather than from a template. The privacy notice names all five forms and the exact fields each asks for, the three suppliers that see the data, and that visitors are set no cookies at all. A change to any public form is a change to that page.

nodes.label: ToFill Markers
nodes.rationale: Two facts only the journal can supply, the registered legal name and postal address, are marked in a bordered maroon box on /privacy and /terms. Search for ToFill.

nodes.label: Highwire Press citation_* Tags
nodes.rationale: What Google Scholar reads. Values are emitted only when known: no ISSN tag while the ISSN is pending, no page numbers until an article has them. sitemap.xml is generated from the content layer.

nodes.label: Admin Panel (editor-facing)
nodes.rationale: Written for an editor, not a developer. Web addresses are written from the title, not typed, and only authors and articles show a URL because they are the only records with a public page. Status wording follows the status until somebody edits it. Order is set with arrows. A rejected save comes back to the form with everything still in it rather than putting Postgres text on an error page. Four inboxes are triaged, never edited.

nodes.label: Runtime Security Model
nodes.rationale: RLS default-denies; anon gets SELECT only on published rows, and submissions/newsletter_subscribers have no public policy at all. Every write goes through a server action on the service-role key guarded by a server-only import so exposing it is a build error. ADMIN_PATH is a second layer, not the control: the session check is, and middleware plus per-page re-checks are both required because middleware does not protect a direct POST.

nodes.label: ADMIN_PATH Route Obscurity
nodes.rationale: Middleware rewrites /{ADMIN_PATH}/* to the internal /admin/* tree; a direct request to /admin/* 404s. Changing the path is a config change, not a code change.

nodes.label: Netlify Deployment Configuration
nodes.rationale: Next inlines every NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable at build time, so adding them changes nothing until a Clear-cache-and-deploy. Until then the admin answers 503 and public pages quietly serve seed content. Do not tick 'Contains secret values' on the three inlined variables: netlify.toml exempts them by name but an explicit UI marking wins over the file. Tick it on SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and RESEND_API_KEY, which must keep failing the build if they ever appear in output.

nodes.label: Mobile Nav Arrives After Hydration
nodes.rationale: The two nav variants are different DOM switched by matchMedia, per the prototype, so a phone is served the desktop bar and swaps to the menu button once JavaScript runs. Rendering both and hiding one with a media query would remove the shift, at the cost of the 'replaces the links' behaviour the chrome tests assert.

nodes.label: Still Open (photographs, real authors, article bodies)
nodes.rationale: Article bodies render placeholder prose: the body column still holds rich-text JSON but the admin no longer exposes it, because it was a monospace box demanding raw JSON that threw a 500 on anything else and fed a renderer that does not exist. A WYSIWYG editor writing that column is the remaining piece. The home image band was removed because it held a placeholder nobody intended to fill. middleware.ts should become proxy.ts: Next 16 deprecated the filename.

nodes.label: Branch Policy (rebuild vs main)
nodes.rationale: Rebuild work lives on rebuild; main still serves the earlier site until this one is ready to go live.
